features.title: Fetch public X post, photos, video samples, and thread posts
features.summary: Fetch a public post, quote, multiple photos, same-author thread follow-ups, and content-aware video samples with bounded frame and media budgets.
failureModes: Only HTTPS x.com and twitter.com status URLs are accepted; private, deleted, or unavailable posts cannot be retrieved.
The third-party FxEmbed API, pbs.twimg.com and video.twimg.com may be unavailable or return unsupported data; failed media is reported alongside available context.
At most 12 same-author follow-up posts and eight media items are processed within 100 seconds; photos are capped at 10 MB and video downloads at 25 MB and 10 minutes.

Video scans at up to 2 FPS over a default 60-second window, then selects distinct sharp frames with temporal coverage; maxFrames defaults to 12 and is capped at 24. ffmpeg must be on the DSH Host PATH, with frames capped at 16 million pixels and single allocations at 128 MB.
Only sampled still images are returned; frame times are approximate and audio and continuous motion are unavailable.

externalDependencies.boundary: The public numeric post ID is sent to api.fxtwitter.com; the thread response supplies post, quote, and thread text, author metadata, and media URLs.
externalDependencies.deterministicFake: The host and media tests provide a FetchHttpClient.Fetch stand-in that answers with a fixed FxEmbed-shaped response; the plugin's HttpClient, size limits and decoding run for real and no public post API is called.

externalDependencies.boundary: Photos are downloaded from pbs.twimg.com and saved as image attachments.
externalDependencies.deterministicFake: The media tests answer pbs.twimg.com through the same Fetch stand-in and verify host and redirect restrictions.

externalDependencies.boundary: An MP4 variant is downloaded from video.twimg.com and decoded by the Host's ffmpeg binary.
externalDependencies.deterministicFake: The host test answers a video.twimg.com URL with a generated two-second local MP4, then uses the real download, temp-file and ffmpeg sampling path.

features.title: Read the timing and key frames of a local video or GIF animation
features.summary: Analyse a local screen recording, video or animated GIF: a still/motion timeline, each motion's start, duration, moving region, progress samples with the nearest CSS timing function or loop period, and key frames as images, so an Agent can rebuild the animation in code.
failureModes: Only a local file is read: a relative path resolves from the thread folder; a missing path, a folder, a file over 100 MB, a file ffmpeg cannot decode and a file without a video stream are refused with what to pass instead.

At most 60 seconds are analysed per call, scanned at no more than 30 FPS, the source frame rate and 300 frames; timings are accurate to one scan frame, a long window lowers the scan rate, and a clip that does not report its length is read up to 300 scan frames with a warning giving the startSeconds to continue from.

Motion is measured from pixel changes on a 128 px scan: progress is a proxy for position, scale or opacity, not a distance; changes below the noise threshold and single-frame palette blips are ignored; transparency is flattened.

maxFrames defaults to 12 and is capped at 24; motions that do not fit keep their timings and are reported in a warning. ffmpeg must be on the DSH Host PATH, with frames capped at 16 million pixels and single allocations at 128 MB.

externalDependencies.boundary: The Host's ffmpeg binary probes, scans and extracts frames from the local file through the DSH subprocess provider, with the file protocol only.
externalDependencies.deterministicFake: Tests generate their reference clips with ffmpeg's lavfi sources (a box with a known position over time) and run the real probe, scan and extraction; a spawner stand-in reports a missing binary.
